zh.summary: NetBIOS／RPC 列舉：區分名稱線索、端點映射、連線與指定操作權限。

sourceBody.text: CEH M04-05｜NetBIOS／RPC：查到名稱與端點，離取得權限還差什麼？
本單元簡短複習 NetBIOS 名稱表與 RPC 端點，再練習分辨「資訊查得到、連線接得上、指定操作獲准」三種不同證據。
一、先把三種角色放回正確位置

items: NetBIOS（Network Basic Input/Output System）：原本是區域網路程式使用名稱與交換資料的一套介面；放在 TCP/IP 上運作，稱為 NBT 或 NetBT。
SMB（Server Message Block）：讓用戶端存取網路上的檔案等資源。上一課已分開共用清單、目錄清單、讀取及修改權限。
RPC（Remote Procedure Call，遠端程序呼叫）：程式把參數傳給另一個程序，請它執行指定功能，再接收結果。不是遠端桌面，也不等於拿到命令列。

sourceBody.text: 可以把 NetBIOS 名稱想成通訊錄裡的名稱，RPC 端點想成承辦窗口的位置，特定操作權限則是窗口願不願意替這個身分辦理某件事。這只是角色比喻，不是 NetBIOS、SMB、RPC 必須依序執行的固定流程。[RFC 1001：NetBIOS over TCP/IP](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1001)｜[Microsoft：RPC 如何運作](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/rpc/how-rpc-works)
二、NetBIOS 的短複習：看名稱、尾碼與類型，不把它當成權限表

在常見 Windows NetBIOS 命名慣例中，名稱共 16 位元組，前 15 位元組放名稱，最後一個位元組是用途尾碼；較短的名稱會補空白。尾碼是十六進位數值，不是連接埠號碼。[Microsoft：NetBIOS 名稱表示法](https://learn.microsoft.com/zh-tw/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-brws/940f299f-669f-4a0b-8411-9ead7e2f31ec)
例如合成名稱表中的三筆資料：

items: LAB-FS <00> UNIQUE：工作站服務使用的電腦名稱線索。
LAB-FS <20> UNIQUE：伺服器服務的名稱線索，可引導後續檔案分享查核。
LABGROUP <00> GROUP：群組名稱線索，實際工作群組或網域歸屬仍須核對。

sourceBody.text: UNIQUE 與 GROUP 描述 NetBIOS 名稱類型；GROUP 不是檔案存取控制中的使用者群組。名稱表也不是完整帳號清單。看到 <20>，不能直接推出共用名稱、SMB 版本或指定檔案的讀取權限。[Microsoft：名稱與尾碼行為](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-nbte/6dbf0972-bb15-4f29-afeb-baaae98416ed)

常見連接埠角色可一起複習：名稱服務使用 UDP／TCP 137、資料報服務使用 UDP 138、工作階段服務使用 TCP 139；直接透過 TCP 的 SMB 使用 445，可不依賴 NetBIOS。因此，137 沒有回應，不代表 445 上的 SMB 一定不存在。[Microsoft：NetBIOS 與直接 SMB 傳輸](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/networking/direct-hosting-of-smb-over-tcpip)
Windows 的 nbtstat 也要分清資料從哪裡來：

items: nbtstat /n：本機名稱表。
nbtstat /c：本機名稱快取，可能反映先前解析結果。
nbtstat /a LAB-FS：依遠端名稱查名稱表。
nbtstat /A 192.0.2.10：依 IP 查遠端名稱表。

sourceBody.text: /a 與 /A 大小寫有差別。最後一例的 IP 是文件示範位址，不是本課測試目標；這裡不需要執行指令。另注意 /R、/RR 會清除／重載快取或重新註冊名稱，不是單純顯示資訊的同義選項。[Microsoft：nbtstat](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/nbtstat)
三、RPC 多分一層：介面、操作與端點
RPC 裡的三個名詞回答不同問題：

items: 介面（Interface）：提供哪一組約定好的功能與參數格式。
操作（Operation／Procedure）：這次要呼叫哪一個具體功能，例如讀取某項狀態。
端點（Endpoint）：透過哪個通訊位置連到服務。TCP 端點可以是埠號；具名管道端點則是管道名稱，不是另一個 TCP 埠。

sourceBody.text: Microsoft RPC 介面常以 UUID（通用唯一識別碼）和介面版本識別。這個版本描述介面的相容契約，不能直接當成 Windows 或應用程式產品版本，更不能只拿版本數字套用 CVE。[Microsoft：RPC 介面識別](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/rpcdce/ns-rpcdce-rpc_if_id)｜[端點的種類](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/rpc/finding-endpoints)
Endpoint Mapper（端點對應服務）像查號臺：協助把要找的介面對應到通訊位置。它回覆位置，不會替呼叫者核發所有功能的使用權。

常見 Microsoft RPC over TCP 情境是：先向 TCP 135 的 Endpoint Mapper 查詢，再連到回傳的服務埠。現代 Windows 常見的動態 TCP 埠範圍是 49152–65535，但實際服務可能採固定埠或另有設定；不能把這段範圍當成每台設備的實測結果，也不是一律對外全開的設定建議。[Microsoft：服務與網路連接埠需求](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/networking/service-overview-and-network-port-requirements)

也有 RPC 經由 SMB 的具名管道傳輸，或用戶端已知道端點的情況，所以不是每次 RPC 呼叫都必須先經過 TCP 135。Samba 的 rpcclient 是 MS-RPC 用戶端工具，可以使用具名管道或 TCP 等傳輸；工具叫 rpcclient，不表示它的每個命令都只查詢資料，還要核對具體子命令。[Samba：rpcclient](https://www.samba.org/samba/docs/current/man-html/rpcclient.1.html)
四、111 與 135：同樣協助找服務，但不是同一套協定

ONC RPC 常見於 Unix／Linux 相關服務，使用 program number（程式編號）、version（服務協定版本）與 procedure number（程序編號）識別服務及操作。rpcbind／portmapper 在 TCP／UDP 上使用 111，協助查找服務位址；這與 Microsoft RPC 的介面 UUID、TCP 135 不是同一套查詢格式。[RFC 5531：ONC RPC](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc5531/)｜[RFC 1833：ONC RPC 對應協定](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1833)
常見的 rpcinfo 可查詢 ONC RPC 登記資料，不能因名稱相似就拿來代替 Microsoft RPC 工具；它也有其他操作選項，使用前仍須核對參數。[Oracle：rpcinfo 官方手冊](https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E88353_01/html/E72487/rpcinfo-8.html)
也別把「先問 111，再連 NFS」背成所有版本的通則。NFSv4.1 規格以 2049 為預設服務埠，並建議用戶端不要使用上述 RPC binding 查詢流程。不用 rpcbind，不代表不用 RPC；NFS 的版本差異下一單元再展開。[RFC 8881 §2.9.3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8881.html#section-2.9.3)
五、這次的新重點：失敗發生在哪一步？
看 RPC 測試結果，可以分成以下問題；它們不是每次都要從頭重做的固定清單：

items: 取得登記資料了嗎？查到端點只是取得映射資訊，尚未證明從目前位置能連到它。
端點可達嗎？映射服務有回應，實際服務埠仍可能被防火牆擋住、停止監聽或已變動。

介面相容嗎？即使 TCP 連線成功，RPC bind 仍要確認介面與傳輸語法等條件。這裡的 bind 是建立 RPC 通訊約定，不是「取得管理權限」。[Microsoft：版本與能力協商](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-rpce/ed7bf5ae-ec8e-407e-b6d7-663958e18701)
以什麼身分要求哪個操作？身分驗證處理呼叫者身分，授權處理能否執行指定工作；某個查詢成功，不能擴張成所有操作都獲准。[Microsoft：RPC 安全的基本原則](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/rpc/rpc-security-essentials)

sourceBody.text: 所以「沒有回應」不能直接寫成帳號密碼錯誤，「介面無法使用」不能直接寫成被防火牆擋住，「Access Denied」也不能直接寫成整台主機都安全。先保存原始錯誤、目標、傳輸、身分與發生階段，再配合管理端設定及日誌確認原因。
只阻擋查號臺，不一定阻止已知端點的呼叫；只保護其中一個埠，也未必涵蓋其他傳輸。防護要一起看映射服務、實際端點、可連線來源及操作權限。若確定沒有舊系統依賴，再經相容性測試停用 NetBIOS；不要為了消除 135 埠就隨意停用 Windows 核心 RPC 服務。
六、用一份合成紀錄練習寫結論
以下是紙上案例，沒有查詢任何真實主機。假設測試已核准，紀錄如下：

items: Lab-A 的 NetBIOS 名稱表回傳 LAB-FS <20> UNIQUE。
Lab-A 的 Endpoint Mapper 回傳：某個 RPC 介面版本 1.0 登記在 TCP 50020。
從同一個測試網段連到 TCP 50020 時逾時，未進行該端點的 RPC 呼叫。
沒有查詢 SMB 共用，也沒有讀取任何檔案。

sourceBody.text: 可以記錄：「本次取得 Lab-A 的伺服器服務名稱線索及一筆 RPC 端點映射；從指定測試位置連向 TCP 50020 逾時，尚未驗證該端點的介面呼叫、身分驗證或操作權限。SMB 共用與檔案存取均未測試。」
這個記錄保留了已觀察與未知的界線。實際工作再附上時間、工具版本、完整參數及原始回應，避免把密碼或無關個資寫進報告。若要繼續測試，先確認核准範圍包括該端點與指定唯讀操作；不能因為查到了新埠，就自動擴大測試。
今天只做一個小檢核
同事看完上述紀錄說：「<20> 表示共享檔案能讀；135 已經回傳介面，所以我們有 RPC 管理權；50020 逾時，證明那項服務不存在。」
請用兩三句話修正這段結論，指出已確認的資訊、尚不能下的結論，以及下一步應核對的證據。
這次只需判讀合成資料，不用連線、安裝工具或改設定，因此沒有環境清理操作。下一單元接 Unix／Linux 使用者與 NFS。

paragraphs: 目前只確認取得 LAB-FS 的 <20> 伺服器服務名稱線索，以及某 RPC 介面版本 1.0 對應 TCP 50020 的登記資料；這些都不證明可以讀共享檔案或具備管理權限。50020 逾時只表示本次連線未在等待時間內成功，原因與服務是否仍存在還不能確定，RPC 呼叫、驗證及操作權限也都尚未測試。下一步應在核准範圍內核對端點目前的監聽與映射、路徑／防火牆和日誌；若要驗證檔案讀取或 RPC 功能，須以已核准身分分別測試指定操作。
判讀重點：名稱線索、登記資料、端點連線與操作權限各有自己的證據；沒有測試的項目保留未知。這是編輯參考解答，不是學員實際作答或精熟證據。

en.summary: NetBIOS/RPC enumeration: distinguish name clues, endpoint mappings, connections, and permission for specified operations.

sourceBody.text: CEH M04-05 | NetBIOS/RPC: what separates discovering names and endpoints from obtaining permission?

This fifth unit briefly reviews NetBIOS name tables and RPC endpoints, then distinguishes three kinds of evidence: information was returned, a connection succeeded, and a specified operation was authorized.
1. Put the three roles in context

items: NetBIOS (Network Basic Input/Output System): originally an interface for local-network programs to use names and exchange data. Its operation over TCP/IP is called NBT or NetBT.
SMB (Server Message Block): lets clients access files and other resources over a network. The preceding lesson distinguishes share lists, directory lists, reading, and modification permissions.
RPC (Remote Procedure Call): a program passes parameters to another process, requests a specified function, and receives a result. This is not remote desktop access or possession of a command shell.

sourceBody.text: Think of a NetBIOS name as a name in a directory, an RPC endpoint as the location of a service counter, and operation permission as whether that counter will perform a particular task for this identity. This is a role analogy, not a mandatory NetBIOS → SMB → RPC sequence. [RFC 1001: NetBIOS over TCP/IP](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1001) | [Microsoft: How RPC works](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/rpc/how-rpc-works)
2. NetBIOS review: names, suffixes, and types are not a permission table

Under common Windows NetBIOS naming conventions, a name has 16 bytes: the first 15 contain the name, and the final byte is a purpose suffix. Shorter names are padded with spaces. The suffix is a hexadecimal value, not a port number. [Microsoft: NetBIOS name representation](https://learn.microsoft.com/zh-tw/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-brws/940f299f-669f-4a0b-8411-9ead7e2f31ec)
For example, a synthetic name table contains these three records:

items: LAB-FS <00> UNIQUE: a computer-name clue used by the workstation service.
LAB-FS <20> UNIQUE: a server-service name clue that can guide later file-sharing checks.
LABGROUP <00> GROUP: a group-name clue; actual workgroup or domain membership still needs checking.

sourceBody.text: UNIQUE and GROUP describe NetBIOS name types. GROUP is not a user group in file access control. A name table is not a complete account list either. Seeing <20> does not establish share names, the SMB version, or permission to read a particular file. [Microsoft: Names and suffix behavior](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-nbte/6dbf0972-bb15-4f29-afeb-baaae98416ed)

Review the usual port roles together: the name service uses UDP/TCP 137, the datagram service UDP 138, and the session service TCP 139. Direct SMB over TCP uses 445 and can operate without NetBIOS. Thus, no response on 137 does not establish that SMB on 445 is absent. [Microsoft: NetBIOS and direct SMB transport](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/networking/direct-hosting-of-smb-over-tcpip)
With Windows nbtstat, distinguish where the information comes from:

items: nbtstat /n: the local name table.
nbtstat /c: the local name cache, which may reflect earlier resolution results.
nbtstat /a LAB-FS: query a remote name table by remote name.
nbtstat /A 192.0.2.10: query a remote name table by IP address.

sourceBody.text: /a and /A are case-sensitive. The final IP is a documentation example, not a target for this lesson; no command execution is needed here. Also, /R and /RR clear/reload the cache or re-register names; they are not synonyms for merely displaying information. [Microsoft: nbtstat](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/nbtstat)
3. Distinguish RPC interfaces, operations, and endpoints
Three RPC terms answer different questions:

items: Interface: which agreed set of functions and parameter formats is offered?
Operation/Procedure: which specific function is being called this time, such as reading a particular status?
Endpoint: which communication location reaches the service? A TCP endpoint can be a port number; a named-pipe endpoint is a pipe name, not another TCP port.

sourceBody.text: Microsoft RPC interfaces are commonly identified by a UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) and an interface version. That version describes an interface compatibility contract. It is not directly a Windows or application product version, and a version number alone cannot establish CVE applicability. [Microsoft: RPC interface identification](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/rpcdce/ns-rpcdce-rpc_if_id) | [Endpoint types](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/rpc/finding-endpoints)
The Endpoint Mapper is like directory assistance: it maps the desired interface to a communication location. Returning a location does not grant the caller permission to use every function.

A common Microsoft RPC over TCP case queries the Endpoint Mapper on TCP 135, then connects to the returned service port. Modern Windows commonly uses the dynamic TCP range 49152–65535, but an actual service may use a fixed port or another configuration. This range is neither a measured result for every device nor a recommendation to expose all those ports externally. [Microsoft: Service and network port requirements](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/networking/service-overview-and-network-port-requirements)

RPC can also use SMB named pipes, or a client may already know the endpoint, so not every RPC call must first pass through TCP 135. Samba's rpcclient is an MS-RPC client that can use named-pipe or TCP transports. Its name does not mean that every command only queries information; inspect the specific subcommand as well. [Samba: rpcclient](https://www.samba.org/samba/docs/current/man-html/rpcclient.1.html)
4. Ports 111 and 135 help locate services using different protocols

ONC RPC is common in Unix/Linux-related services. It identifies services and operations using a program number, version (service protocol version), and procedure number. rpcbind/portmapper uses TCP/UDP 111 to help locate service addresses. This is not the same query format as Microsoft RPC interface UUIDs and TCP 135. [RFC 5531: ONC RPC](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc5531/) | [RFC 1833: ONC RPC binding protocols](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1833)

The common rpcinfo utility can query ONC RPC registrations. Similar naming does not make it a substitute for Microsoft RPC tools. It also has other operation options, so inspect its arguments before use. [Oracle: rpcinfo manual](https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E88353_01/html/E72487/rpcinfo-8.html)

Do not memorize “ask 111, then connect to NFS” as a rule for every version. NFSv4.1 specifies 2049 as the default service port and recommends that clients not use the RPC binding lookup process described above. Not using rpcbind does not mean not using RPC; the next unit explores NFS version differences. [RFC 8881 §2.9.3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8881.html#section-2.9.3)
5. Identify the stage at which a failure occurred
Use these questions to interpret RPC results; they are not a fixed checklist that must restart for every call:

items: Was registration information obtained? Discovering an endpoint only obtains mapping information; it does not establish reachability from the current location.
Is the endpoint reachable? The mapping service can respond while a firewall blocks the actual service port, the service stops listening, or its location changes.

Is the interface compatible? Even after a TCP connection succeeds, RPC bind must establish conditions such as the interface and transfer syntax. Here, bind establishes an RPC communication agreement; it does not mean obtaining administrative permission. [Microsoft: Version and capability negotiation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-rpce/ed7bf5ae-ec8e-407e-b6d7-663958e18701)

Which identity is requesting which operation? Authentication concerns the caller's identity; authorization concerns permission to perform a specified task. One successful query does not establish permission for every operation. [Microsoft: RPC security essentials](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/rpc/rpc-security-essentials)

sourceBody.text: Thus, “no response” does not directly establish incorrect credentials, “interface unavailable” does not directly establish a firewall block, and “Access Denied” does not establish that the entire host is secure. Preserve the original error, target, transport, identity, and failure stage, then correlate administrative configuration and logs to identify the cause.

Blocking directory assistance alone may not stop calls to known endpoints. Protecting one port may not cover other transports. Defense must consider the mapping service, actual endpoints, permitted connection sources, and operation permissions together. Disable NetBIOS only after confirming there are no legacy dependencies and testing compatibility. Do not casually disable core Windows RPC services merely to eliminate port 135.
6. Practice a conclusion using a synthetic record
This is a tabletop case; no real host was queried. Assume testing was authorized and the record says:

items: Lab-A's NetBIOS name table returned LAB-FS <20> UNIQUE.
Lab-A's Endpoint Mapper returned a registration mapping an RPC interface version 1.0 to TCP 50020.
A connection to TCP 50020 from the same test subnet timed out; no RPC call was made to that endpoint.
No SMB shares were queried and no files were read.

sourceBody.text: A suitable record is: “This test obtained a server-service name clue and an RPC endpoint mapping for Lab-A. The connection from the specified test location to TCP 50020 timed out; interface calls, authentication, and operation permissions at that endpoint remain unverified. SMB shares and file access were not tested.”

This record preserves the boundary between observations and unknowns. In actual work, also retain the time, tool version, full arguments, and original response, while keeping passwords and unrelated personal information out of the report. Before continuing, confirm that the approved scope includes that endpoint and the specified read-only operation. Discovering a new port does not automatically expand testing scope.
One small check

A colleague reads the record and says: “<20> means shared files are readable; 135 returned an interface, so we have RPC administrative permission; the timeout on 50020 proves that service does not exist.”
Correct this conclusion in two or three sentences. Identify what was confirmed, which conclusions remain unsupported, and the evidence to check next.
This task only interprets synthetic data. It requires no connection, tool installation, or configuration change, so there is no environment cleanup. The next unit covers Unix/Linux users and NFS.

paragraphs: The only confirmed observations are a LAB-FS <20> server-service name clue and registration data mapping an RPC interface version 1.0 to TCP 50020. Neither proves shared-file read access or administrative permission. A timeout on 50020 only means this connection did not succeed within the waiting period; its cause and the service's continued existence remain undetermined, and RPC calls, authentication, and operation permissions have not been tested. Within the approved scope, next check the endpoint's current listener and mapping, network path/firewall, and logs. Testing file reads or RPC functionality requires separate tests of specified operations using an approved identity.

Interpretation principle: name clues, registrations, endpoint connections, and operation permissions each require their own evidence. Untested items remain unknown. This is an editorial reference answer, not an actual learner response or evidence of mastery.
